findings.claim: The size bound is enforced only against Lstat's Size, never against the bytes ReadFile returns. A file that grows between Lstat and ReadFile, or a reader whose Size disagrees with its bytes, passes MaxSourceBytes unbounded. A Text request is not bounded by MaxSourceBytes at all, so only the MaxChunks error limits it. Re-checking len(data) against the limit would close the gap.
proof_refs: extract.go:84-111 never consults MaxSourceBytes for Text

findings.claim: Any Lstat failure becomes a request error. This includes permission denied on a parent directory, which is a per-item failure equivalent to the 'unreadable' skip code. A single-file request therefore reports a hard error where ReadFile's failure reports a skip. The split is undocumented and untested. The only Lstat error the tests cover is not-exist.
proof_refs: extract_test.go TestExtractRefusesAPathThatIsNotAFile covers only the missing-path case
extract.go:155-157 maps a ReadFile error to a skip

findings.claim: origin.Kind is overwritten with KindFile after validate accepted KindDirectory for a Path request. A caller who passes KindDirectory with a file Path is silently reclassified, so the topic key becomes ingested/file/... instead of the kind the caller asked for. Either validate should require KindFile for a non-directory path, or the rewrite should be documented.
proof_refs: validate accepts KindFile or KindDirectory when Path is set

findings.claim: The 'empty' skip for a pasted-text request, whose Path comes from skipPath's Label branch, is untested. Every 'empty' case in the tests goes through a file. A regression in the Label fallback would pass the suite. The string(data) of a file is also never checked for valid UTF-8 before it enters Record.Content. Only the NUL sniff applies.
proof_refs: extract_test.go TestExtractSkipsWhatOneFileCannotYield has file cases only
